chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'By what sign is the believer known to be a believer?' He said, 'By submission to Allah and contentment with whatever befalls him, whether joy or anger.'
ai.seo_question: How can one recognize a true believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the hallmark of a true believer as 'al-taslim' (complete submission) and 'al-rida' (contentment) with Allah's decree, demonstrating spiritual maturity by maintaining equanimity in both joy and hardship. This hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the Shia concept that faith is not merely belief but a state of inner peace that accepts divine wisdom regardless of whether the outcome is perceived as pleasant or difficult.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from the one who mentioned it,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘By which thing does the Momin know that he is a Momin?’ Heasws said: ‘By the submission to Allahazwj, and the satisfaction regarding whatever traspires upon him, from the joy or anger’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated from him from his father from ibn Sinan from those whom he has mentioned from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“I (the narrator) asked him, (abu ‘Abd Allah, recipient of divine supreme covenant), ‘By what means can a believer know that he is a believer?’ The Imam said, ‘(He can find out) by means of his submitting himself to Allah, and agreeing with whatever happiness or sadness that he may experience.’”
